newsitem.title: GERMANY: CHINA EYES GLOBAL RAPESEED MARKET - GERMAN TRADE.
newsitem.headline: CHINA EYES GLOBAL RAPESEED MARKET - GERMAN TRADE.

text.p: Chinese buyers are eyeing international rapeseed markets as they seek to cover protein demand ahead of soybean crops in the autumn, German traders said.
European prices were holding firm, which might help Canada to sell from its huge 1997/98 canola crop.
"I think it will be more likely that China buys Canadian rapeseed rather than European origin, because it is too expensive," one broker said.
"New crop rapeseed seems to be holding firm and local crushers already can't lay their hands on Sept/Oct supply, so overseas buyers will have even more of a problem."
Europe's new crop is expected to exceed eight million tonnes after 7.14 million last year, but prices are holding around 440 marks a tonne free Hamburg.
A year ago, when Germany was expecting to lose a third of its rapeseed crop due to winter damage, the new crop price was 445 marks.
Oct/Nov prices fob Baltic are at 470 marks.
The strength of the market reflects a combination of buoyant world oilseeds demand and a firm dollar.
Asian crops may be reduced by the El Nino weather phenomenon, while in Germany rapeseed prices are also being boosted by hoarding.
"About one quarter of the German crop has been sold to processors ahead of the harvest and the rest will be firmly locked away," a trader said.
"Crushers will need fresh supply at the end of September."
China is due to harvest some nine million tonnes after 9.1 million last year and could seek to import between 500,000 and one million tonnes of rapeseed, he added.
The U.S. Agriculture Department on Tuesday said China's oilseed output was slipping.
